## Direction 1 — "The Painted Sign"
**Concept:** Built directly from your storefront — the weathered cream paint, dark green lettering, and the feeling that someone mixed the paint by hand and lettered it on a slow afternoon.

This is the required "extends your existing brand" direction.

### Typography
| Role | Font | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Display (headings, prices, the bakery name) | **Cormorant Garamond** (Google Fonts) | High stroke contrast — the thick-to-thin variation mimics brush pressure, the same movement that made your sign. Feels hand-applied without being a novelty font. |
| Body (item descriptions, instructions) | **Lato** (Google Fonts) | Genuinely warm for a sans-serif — the rounded terminals (the ends of letter strokes) don't feel cold. Lets Cormorant breathe instead of competing. |

### Color
| Hex | Role |
|---|---|
| `#F5F0E8` | Background — warm cream, like the sign's paint in daylight |
| `#EAE4D6` | Surface — for cards, the order panel; one shade deeper than background so items lift without a harsh border |
| `#1A2B18` | Primary text — your dark green pulled to near-black so it reads at night on a dim phone screen |
| `#6B7A62` | Muted text — sage, the midpoint between your green and cream; used for subtitles, help text |
| `#C08B3A` | Accent — bread-crust amber. Appears *only* on the "Add to order" button and the final total. Nowhere else. |
| `#A83226` | Alert — deep terracotta, for errors and "item sold out" states |

### Shape Language
- **Corner radius:** 4 px everywhere. Not square, not pill-shaped — like wood that's been lightly sanded. Hand-cut.
- **Borders over shadows:** 1 px solid in `#6B7A62` on cards. Shadows suggest digital depth; borders suggest something drawn.
- **Density:** Balanced. Each item gets room. This is not a menu crammed on a fridge magnet.

### Signature Element
Wheat stalk dividers — your logo element, used as a thin horizontal rule between sections (not decorative, structural). It means every page section is implicitly "signed" by the bakery without repeating the full logo.

### Where It Could Go Wrong
The chalkboard interior is a temptation — if anyone adds a chalk texture, a dark background section, or a "specials" slate, it tips immediately into a Yelp-listing cliché. Keep the palette in the cream-and-green space only; leave the chalkboard inside the building.

---

## Direction 2 — "Papier Timbré"
*Papier timbré* is a French term for stamped paper — literally a document made official with a single ink mark.

**Concept:** The visual language of a French village boulangerie (bakery) where your order was written on a kraft paper form and stamped with the baker's mark. Every interaction is a small, quiet ceremony.

### Typography
| Role | Font | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Display | **Libre Baskerville** (Google Fonts) | Sturdy, from the American revival of an old letterpress (physical printing press) tradition. It has ink spread baked into its proportions — letters that look like they were pressed into paper. |
| Body | **Crimson Pro** (Google Fonts) | A reading serif — designed for long-form text. Its humanist (shaped like hand-drawn letters) proportions complement Libre Baskerville without matching it exactly; you get two friends, not twins. |

### Color
| Hex | Role |
|---|---|
| `#F0E8D5` | Background — kraft paper, warm ochre-beige |
| `#FBF7EE` | Surface — near-white unbleached paper, for cards |
| `#231810` | Primary text — very dark brown, ink on paper |
| `#8C7A62` | Muted text — aged, faded ink; for secondary labels |
| `#1F3D12` | Accent — the baker's stamp green. Used *once*: the confirmation stamp on the order summary screen. Nowhere else on the journey. |
| `#B03020` | Alert — sold out, errors |

### Shape Language
- **Corner radius:** 2 px — nearly square. This is a paper form, not a consumer app.
- **Borders, not shadows:** 1 px in `#8C7A62`. Everything reads as flat printed matter.
- **Density:** Airy. Forms have space to breathe; each item is a line entry with room around it.

### Signature Element
One single stamp graphic — the wheat stalk drawn in a circle, as if pressed by a rubber stamp — appears *only* on the order confirmation screen. It's the moment the order becomes real. Used nowhere else in the product.

### Where It Could Go Wrong
The very pale palette is clean in daylight but can feel thin and cold on a phone screen in a dark room. If the contrast ratios (the difference in brightness between text and background) aren't pushed far enough, it becomes hard to read at night — exactly when your customers are using it. The `#231810` on `#FBF7EE` combination passes, but it needs to be tested under real conditions.

---

## Direction 3 — "Recipe Hand"
**Concept:** The UI (user interface — the screens the customer interacts with) is composed like a handwritten index card recipe — items listed like ingredients, the order form like a method, the confirmation like the finished dish. Rooted in the private, personal language of a recipe passed down through a family.

### Typography
| Role | Font | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Display | **Caveat** (Google Fonts) | A clean handwriting font — unlike most handwriting fonts, Caveat is actually legible at display sizes because it doesn't try to fake cursive. It looks written, not printed, which is the whole point of this direction. |
| Body | **Atkinson Hyperlegible** (Google Fonts) | Designed by the Braille Institute specifically for people with low vision reading in poor light — which is a perfect description of your users (phone, couch, nighttime). It has a slightly imperfect, humanist quality that doesn't feel clinical. |

### Color
| Hex | Role |
|---|---|
| `#FAF6EF` | Background — recipe card cream, aged but not yellow |
| `#F0EBE1` | Surface — the card itself, slightly warmer; gives items a lifted feel |
| `#2A1E12` | Primary text — dark brown ink |
| `#9A8878` | Muted text — pencil-grey brown, for secondary labels |
| `#DDD4C4` | Line color — ruled lines appear faintly behind text areas, like a lined index card |
| `#2C6E49` | Accent — a herb green, used *only* for the "added ✓" confirmation state. A visual equivalent of a green pen tick. |
| `#9B3922` | Alert — red ink, like circling a mistake |

### Shape Language
- **Corner radius:** 8 px on cards — softened corners from years of handling, edges slightly worn.
- **Shadows, not borders:** Soft, warm-toned drop shadows (not grey) suggest paper lifted slightly off a surface.
- **Density:** Balanced. Recipe cards pack information but leave room for the eye to move.

### Signature Element
The order list is styled as an ingredient list. The checkout screen reads: *"Recipe for Wednesday morning: 1 sourdough loaf, 2 almond croissants, 1 pain au chocolat."* It reframes the transaction as something personal and made-for-you, not a ticket number.

### Where It Could Go Wrong
Caveat becomes illegible at small sizes, especially if someone uses a small default font in their phone's accessibility settings. The handwriting frame can also make first-time visitors uncertain whether they're in the right place — it reads as personal before it reads as functional. This direction needs especially careful work on button states and labels to stay usable.

---

## My Recommendation

**Go with Direction 1, but borrow the stamp moment from Direction 2.**

Your existing brand is genuinely good — a cream-and-dark-green hand-painted sign is not something to move away from, it's something most bakeries wish they had. Direction 1 is the only one that makes a first-time visitor say "this is *that* bakery" the moment they land. The amber accent keeps it from feeling like a retro template, and the 4 px radius strikes exactly the right balance between handmade and usable on a phone. Stealing the single rubber-stamp confirmation from Direction 2 costs nothing and adds the one moment of ceremony this type of order genuinely deserves.

# Three Design Directions

---

## Direction 1 — "The Sign Lives Here"
**Concept:** Your physical shop, translated pixel for pixel. The hand-painted cream-on-dark-green sign, the chalkboard, the wheat stalk — a customer who walks past your window every morning should open the app and feel *immediately* that it belongs to the same place.

**Why this is not "just match your brand colors":** The logic here is spatial continuity. The app is a second door into the same room. Every visual choice is borrowed from a real object that already exists in your shop.

### Typography
| Role | Font | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Display (headlines, item names) | **Cormorant Garamond** (Google Fonts) | Old-style serif — meaning thick-to-thin strokes like a good brush — that reads the way a hand-painted sign *looks*. Use Bold weight only. At large sizes it commands attention; it doesn't need decoration. |
| Body / UI text | **Lato** (Google Fonts) | A humanist sans-serif — meaning the letterforms have slight calligraphic origins, not pure geometry — that stays warm without competing with Cormorant. Reads cleanly at 14–16px on a dim phone screen at 10 PM. |

**Term clarified:** *humanist sans-serif* = a letterform style where the underlying shapes come from handwriting tradition rather than compass-and-ruler geometry. Feels warmer than something like Helvetica.

### Color Palette
| Swatch | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 🟫 | `#F7F0DC` | **Background** — aged cream, your sign's base coat |
| ⬜ | `#FDFAF4` | **Surface** — card/menu item backgrounds, slightly lighter |
| 🟩 | `#1E2A1F` | **Text** — very dark forest green instead of pure black; keeps warmth |
| 🌿 | `#6B7A6C` | **Muted text** — for prices, subheadings, placeholder copy |
| 🟠 | `#C4873A` | **Accent** — toasted wheat/amber. Used exactly once: the "Place Order" button. Nowhere else. |
| 🔴 | `#A33328` | **Alert** — "Sold out today" label, form errors |

### Shape Language
- Corner radius: **4px** — barely rounded; feels handmade, not app-template smooth
- Borders over shadows: a `1px` line at `#1E2A1F` at 12% opacity instead of drop shadows; shadows feel digital, borders feel like a menu board edge
- Density: **balanced** — enough breathing room to feel special; tight enough that a full bakery menu isn't a scroll marathon on a phone

### Signature Element
A narrow **dark-green header bar** the width of the screen, with the wheat stalk in cream centered in it — exactly like your sign above the door. It appears on every screen. Customers don't consciously notice it, but it makes every page feel like they're standing under your awning.

### Where It Could Go Wrong
If a developer reaches for a chalk texture overlay — a semi-transparent grain image meant to simulate a chalkboard — it makes the app look like a WordPress theme from 2012 and murders readability at small sizes. The restraint *is* the concept; the moment you add texture, this becomes costume.

---

## Direction 2 — "Wax Paper & Ink"
**Concept:** A French neighborhood *boulangerie* (bakery — a French word for a shop specializing in bread, pronounced *boo-lahn-zhuh-REE*) wraps your loaf in wax paper and stamps the bag with a single mark. Not Ladurée, not a croissant emoji — the rubber stamp on a paper bag from a shop that has been there since 1962 and has no interest in your Instagram feed. This direction is rooted in the *packaging object*, not the shop interior.

**Why this isn't the same as Direction 1:** This one starts from the outside of the French bakery box in your references, not from your own existing shop. The palette shifts to kraft (warm tan), and the mood is drier, more confident, slightly more spare.

### Typography
| Role | Font | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Display | **Playfair Display Bold** (Google Fonts) | At heavy weight, the thick strokes look almost like a woodblock print — the technique where text is carved into wood and pressed with ink — which is exactly the stamp aesthetic. The contrast (thin vs. thick strokes) is extreme, giving it presence without needing size. |
| Body / UI text | **Crimson Pro** (Google Fonts) | A text-first old-style serif — meaning designed to be read at small sizes, not just displayed large — that keeps the French-stationery feeling without slipping into academic. |

### Color Palette
| Swatch | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 🟤 | `#EDE0C4` | **Background** — kraft paper; warm but not baby-food yellow |
| ⬜ | `#F8F3E8` | **Surface** — lighter page/card inset |
| 🟫 | `#2A1F14` | **Text** — dark brown ink, not black; reads as "stamped" |
| 🌰 | `#8B7355` | **Muted text** — faded ink, secondary information |
| 🟢 | `#1E4D2B` | **Accent** — deep forest green, used *only* on the confirmation "stamp" and the primary CTA. Once. |
| 🔴 | `#7A2020` | **Alert** — deep red, like a "SOLD OUT" rubber stamp |

### Shape Language
- Corner radius: **2px** — almost nothing; the edges of a paper bag aren't rounded
- Borders (not shadows): `1px` solid `#2A1F14` at 10% — like the cut edge of paper stock
- Density: **airy** — wide margins, generous vertical space between items, no visual clutter; this aesthetic earns its authority through *less*

### Signature Element
The order confirmation screen shows a single large green **stamp mark** — a circle with "ORDER CONFIRMED" and the pickup time inside it, styled like an actual rubber stamp (slightly imperfect, ink-pressed). No animation beyond a one-frame opacity fade. No confetti. That stamp dropping on screen is the only celebration you need.

**Term clarified:** *opacity fade* = an element that starts invisible and becomes visible over, say, 200 milliseconds. The opposite of a bounce animation.

### Where It Could Go Wrong
The kraft palette has been strip-mined by every artisan granola brand, cold-brew startup, and sourdough influencer since 2015. The difference is discipline: if a single mason-jar icon or hand-lettered "MADE WITH LOVE" subtitle appears anywhere near this UI, it collapses into cliché immediately. The concept lives or dies on confidence and restraint.

---

## Direction 3 — "From the Recipe Box"
**Concept:** An index card pulled from a wooden recipe box — the yellowed card with ruled lines, written in pencil, passed down. Not the recipe itself, but the *card*: the object you hold, the texture of the ruled lines, the way someone's handwriting abbreviates "tsp" with a period. This is rooted in a domestic object, not a commercial one.

### Typography
| Role | Font | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Display (product names, section headers) | **Caveat** (Google Fonts) | A handwriting-style font — meaning it mimics letterforms drawn by hand — that avoids the twee (overly cute, trying too hard) problem by being slightly irregular without being illegible. Used *only* for product names and the total; never for instructions or fine print. |
| Body / UI text | **Nunito** (Google Fonts) | Rounded humanist sans. *Rounded* means the letter terminals — the ends of strokes — are circular rather than cut flat. This reduces eye strain at night on a bright phone screen, which is the exact moment your users are ordering. |

### Color Palette
| Swatch | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 🟡 | `#FAF6EE` | **Background** — aged paper; close to white but with warmth |
| ⬜ | `#FFFFFF` | **Surface** — pure white card insets, which read as "the card itself" against the warm background |
| 🟫 | `#2D2416` | **Text** — pencil-dark warm brown |
| 🌾 | `#9E8E6F` | **Muted text** — faded pencil, as if the card is a few years old |
| 🟠 | `#C4581A` | **Accent** — rust orange, like old ballpoint pen ink. Used only on the "Add to Order" button. |
| 🔴 | `#8B2A2A` | **Alert** — "sold out" |

### Shape Language
- Corner radius: **10px** — slightly larger than Direction 1; an index card has a small natural curve at the corners
- Shadows (not borders): `box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.07)` — the lift of a physical card sitting on a table, not a digital effect
- Density: **balanced** — each product card feels like its own card in the box; not stacked tightly, not floating in space

### Signature Element
Each product card carries a small **pencil-sketch icon** of that item — a rough croissant outline, a loaf, a cinnamon roll — drawn at roughly 32×32px in the muted text color. Deliberately imperfect, not polished illustration, not clipart. It looks like the margin doodle on the original recipe.

### Where It Could Go Wrong
Caveat is on approximately 40% of farmer's market posters currently in circulation. The moment it appears at body text size, or in a pastel color, the whole direction tips into craft-fair territory and loses the intimacy it's going for. The sketch icons also require an actual illustrator — a free icon set will make this feel like a free WordPress template immediately.

---

# My Recommendation

**I recommend Direction 1, "The Sign Lives Here."**

Your regular customers already have a visual memory tied to that cream-and-dark-green sign — every time they open the app it should confirm *yes, this is the same place*, which builds more trust than a brand-new aesthetic ever could, especially for a transaction (pre-ordering food) where trust matters. Direction 2 is the bolder artistic choice and I'd defend it in a portfolio, but it asks customers to learn a new visual language for a shop they already know; Direction 1 asks nothing of them, it just shows up consistently. The constraint of working within your existing brand isn't a limitation here — the brand is genuinely good, and good material should be used, not replaced.

# TherapyFlow — Spec
*(Working name — no app name was given.)*

---

## 1. One-liner
A booking, payment, and private session-notes tool for a solo licensed therapist and their clients.

---

## 2. Users & Roles

| Role | What they can do | What they must NEVER be able to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Therapist** (1 account, no self-registration) | Set availability; view all appointments; view any client's intake form; write, edit, and read session notes; cancel any appointment; view payment status | Read another therapist's data (N/A, solo); pay for sessions; expose note content to clients |
| **Client** | Create an account; complete intake form; browse open slots; book and pay per session; cancel own appointment; view own upcoming and past appointments; view own intake form | Read session notes — ever, for any session; view other clients' data or intake forms; change the session fee |

---

## 3. The Core Loop

1. Client creates an account (name, email, phone, password).
2. Client completes the intake form (medical history, medications, emergency contact) — required before booking.
3. Client browses the therapist's available time slots and selects one.
4. Client pays by card; the appointment is confirmed only after payment succeeds.
5. Automated text reminders are sent to both parties before the session.
6. Session takes place.
7. Therapist opens the session in their dashboard and writes session notes.
8. Notes auto-save and remain permanently invisible to the client.

---

## 4. Features — V1 (must ship)

**1. Client Account**
*As a client, I want to create an account and log in so that my bookings and health information are tied to my identity.*
- [ ] Sign-up fields: first name, last name, email, mobile phone number, password.
- [ ] Duplicate email shows: "An account with this email already exists."
- [ ] Wrong credentials show: "Email or password is incorrect." (Never say which field is wrong.)
- [ ] Password reset via emailed link.
- [ ] Logged-out users are redirected to Log In if they try to reach any protected screen.

---

**2. Intake Form**
*As a client, I want to submit my medical history and medications before my first session so the therapist has the clinical context they need.*
- [ ] The form is shown automatically after first login and cannot be skipped; booking is blocked until it is submitted.
- [ ] Fields: medical history (multi-line text), current medications (multi-line text), emergency contact name, emergency contact phone number.
- [ ] Client can update the form at any time; each save records a "Last updated" timestamp.
- [ ] Therapist can read any client's intake form from that client's profile — full content, read-only.
- [ ] Client can view their own form but cannot delete it.

---

**3. Availability & Booking**
*As a client, I want to see the therapist's open slots and pick one so I can book without back-and-forth emails.*
- [ ] Therapist adds slots (date, start time, duration, price) from the Availability Settings screen.
- [ ] A slot disappears from the client's view the moment another client books it.
- [ ] If two clients attempt to book the same slot simultaneously, exactly one succeeds; the other sees: "That slot was just taken — please choose another."
- [ ] Slots starting within 24 hours are not shown to clients (matches the cancellation cut-off).
- [ ] A client cannot hold more than one upcoming confirmed booking at a time (V1 simplification; can be relaxed in V2).
- [ ] Empty state (no slots): "No sessions are available right now. Please check back soon."

---

**4. Per-Session Payment**
*As a client, I want to pay for a session at the time of booking so my appointment is confirmed immediately.*
- [ ] Payment is collected at checkout; no appointment is created until payment succeeds.
- [ ] Accepted payment method: credit or debit card.
- [ ] A declined card shows a plain-language error (e.g., "Your card was declined. Please try a different card."); the slot remains open.
- [ ] Client receives an emailed receipt immediately after a successful charge.
- [ ] Therapist sees per-appointment payment status: *paid*, *refunded*, or *cancellation fee charged*.

---

**5. Cancellation Policy**
*As a client, I want to cancel a session, and I understand I will be charged if I cancel less than 24 hours before it starts.*
- [ ] "Cancel" button is visible on the client's Appointment Detail screen for upcoming bookings.
- [ ] A confirmation modal always appears before the cancellation is committed.
- [ ] Cancellation ≥ 24 h before start: full refund issued; slot reopens.
- [ ] Cancellation < 24 h before start: no refund; modal warns "Cancelling less than 24 hours before your session. No refund will be issued." Client must tap "Yes, cancel" to proceed; slot reopens.
- [ ] Therapist can cancel any appointment at any time; full refund is always issued to the client automatically; therapist is never charged a fee.
- [ ] Client receives an SMS when the therapist cancels: "Your session on [date/time] has been cancelled by your therapist. You have been fully refunded."

---

**6. Session Notes**
*As the therapist, I want to write private notes for each session so I maintain a clinical record that clients can never access.*
- [ ] Notes editor is accessible from any appointment in the Therapist Dashboard.
- [ ] Notes auto-save as the therapist types; a "Last saved [time]" indicator is always visible.
- [ ] No client-facing screen, shareable link, or data export ever includes note content.
- [ ] Attempting to access a notes URL while logged in as a client returns a generic "Not found" page — no note content is included in the error response.
- [ ] Notes can be edited at any time by the therapist.
- [ ] Empty state: "No notes yet — start typing to save."

---

**7. Text (SMS) Reminders**
*As a client and as the therapist, I want a text reminder before each session so I don't miss it.*
- [ ] Client receives an SMS 24 hours before the session start: includes date, time, and a cancellation link (active only if ≥ 24 h remain until start).
- [ ] Therapist receives an SMS 1 hour before the session start: includes client name and session time.
- [ ] If a session is cancelled, any queued reminder for that session is suppressed before it sends.
- [ ] An invalid phone number format at sign-up shows an inline error: "Please enter a valid mobile number." Account is not created until corrected.

---

## 5. Features — Later (explicitly NOT in V1)

| Feature | Reason deferred |
|---|---|
| Recurring / package bookings | Changes payment and scheduling logic significantly |
| In-app messaging | Adds a communication and moderation layer |
| Multi-therapist / group practice | Requires multi-tenancy (keeping each therapist's data fully separate) |
| Video / telehealth integration | Third-party dependency; separate product decision |
| Insurance billing / superbill generation | Accounting and compliance layer |
| Client-facing documents or homework | File storage and sharing scope |
| Waitlist for cancelled slots | Scheduling complexity |
| Native mobile app | Web-first for V1 |
| Email reminders | SMS only per spec |
| Multiple active bookings per client | V1 keeps one booking per client; relax once recurring sessions ship |

---

## 6. Screens

### Client-facing

| Screen | Purpose | What's on it | Where you can go from it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sign Up** | Create a client account | Name, email, phone, password fields; submit button | → Intake Form (first time) |
| **Log In** | Authenticate | Email, password; "Forgot password?" link | → Client Dashboard |
| **Intake Form** | Capture health context before first booking | Medical history, medications, emergency contact fields; Save button | → Client Dashboard (after first save) |
| **Client Dashboard** | Client home | Upcoming appointment card (or empty state + "Book a Session" CTA); list of past appointments | → Book a Session, Appointment Detail, Account Settings |
| **Book a Session** | Pick an available slot | Calendar or list of open slots with date, time, duration, price; "Book & Pay" button | → Payment Checkout |
| **Payment Checkout** | Complete payment | Booking summary (date, time, price); card entry form; "Confirm & Pay" button (disabled during processing) | → Booking Confirmation (success) or back to Book a Session (failure) |
| **Booking Confirmation** | Confirm success | Session date/time; reminder info; "Back to Dashboard" button | → Client Dashboard |
| **Appointment Detail** | View one booking | Date, time, status, payment status; "Cancel" button if upcoming | → Cancel Confirmation, Client Dashboard |
| **Cancel Confirmation** | Prevent accidental cancellation | Warning text (fee notice if < 24 h); "Yes, cancel" / "Keep my appointment" | → Client Dashboard |
| **Account Settings** | Manage profile | Editable name and phone; link to view/edit intake form; change password | → Intake Form |

### Therapist-facing

| Screen | Purpose | What's on it | Where you can go from it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Therapist Login** | Authenticate | Email, password; no self-registration link | → Therapist Dashboard |
| **Therapist Dashboard** | Day-at-a-glance | Today's sessions; upcoming sessions list; links to each client | → Session Detail, Client List, Availability Settings |
| **Availability Settings** | Publish open slots | Add/remove slots by date, time, duration, price; list of existing upcoming slots | → Therapist Dashboard |
| **Client List** | Browse all clients | Searchable list; name and last session date | → Client Profile |
| **Client Profile** | View one client | Name, contact info, intake form (read-only), appointment history, payment status per session | → Session Detail, Therapist Dashboard |
| **Session Detail** | Manage one appointment | Date, time, client name, payment status; embedded notes editor; "Cancel" button | → Session Notes (full-screen), Client Profile |
| **Session Notes** | Write clinical notes | Full-screen text editor; auto-save indicator; last-saved timestamp; back button | → Session Detail |

---

## 7. Data

> ⚠️ **Privacy / Legal notice:** This app stores health information (medical history, medications, session notes) and financial reference data. These categories are subject to privacy and healthcare regulations that vary by jurisdiction (for example, HIPAA in the United States). A qualified legal and compliance review **must be completed before launch**. *This is not legal advice.*

| Entity | Fields | Who owns it | Who can read it | Who can edit it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **User** | id, email, password_hash, role *(therapist / client)*, first_name, last_name, phone, created_at | System | Self; Therapist (name + contact only) | Self |
| **Intake Form** | id, client_id, medical_history ⚠️, medications ⚠️, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, updated_at | Client | Therapist (full); Client (own, view only) | Client (updates); Therapist (read-only) |
| **Availability Slot** | id, start_datetime, end_datetime, duration_minutes, price_cents, currency, is_booked, created_at | Therapist | All authenticated users (availability only; price shown at booking) | Therapist |
| **Appointment** | id, client_id, slot_id, status *(scheduled / completed / cancelled / late_cancelled)*, created_at, cancelled_at, cancelled_by | System | Client (own); Therapist (all) | System (status transitions); Therapist (force-cancel) |
| **Payment** | id, appointment_id, client_id, amount_cents, currency, status *(paid / refunded / cancellation_fee_charged)*, payment_provider_reference ⚠️, charged_at | System | Client (own receipt: amount + status); Therapist (status + amount) | System only |
| **Session Note** | id, appointment_id, content ⚠️, last_saved_at, created_at | Therapist | **Therapist only — never client** | Therapist |

⚠️ = **Sensitive field** (health information or financial reference data). Subject to the legal notice above.

---

## 8. Edge Cases & Empty States

1. **No availability set yet** — Client opens "Book a Session" and sees: "No sessions are available right now. Please check back soon." No broken or empty calendar grid is displayed.
2. **First-time client, no bookings** — Client Dashboard shows an empty upcoming card and a prominent "Book your first session" button as the primary action.
3. **Simultaneous booking (race condition** — two users clicking "Book & Pay" at the same time on the same slot**)** — Exactly one booking succeeds; the other receives: "That slot was just taken — please choose another." No double-charge occurs.
4. **Duplicate form submission** — Client taps "Confirm & Pay" twice on a slow connection; the button is disabled after the first tap and only one payment is processed (the second request is **idempotent** — meaning it is safe to receive twice without charging twice).
5. **Payment failure** — Card declined; client sees: "Your card was declined. Please try a different card." Slot remains open; no appointment record is created.
6. **Late cancellation (< 24 h)** — Modal shows: "You are cancelling less than 24 hours before your session. No refund will be issued." Client must explicitly confirm before the cancellation is committed.
7. **Therapist cancels on behalf of client** — Full refund issued automatically; client receives an SMS notification; appointment status updates in both dashboards immediately.
8. **Very long text in notes or intake form** — Fields accept up to 10,000 characters. A soft warning appears at 9,000: "[X] characters remaining." Typing is blocked past the limit.
9. **Invalid phone number at sign-up** — Inline error shown: "Please enter a valid mobile number." Account is not created until the field is corrected.
10. **Client attempts direct URL access to a session note** — Returns a generic "Not found" page; no note content is ever present in the HTTP response, even partially.
11. **Slow network during checkout** — "Confirm & Pay" enters a loading state and is disabled for the duration of processing; the client cannot trigger a second charge.
12. **Therapist opens notes for a session with no notes** — Editor is blank with placeholder text: "No notes yet — start typing to save."

---

## 9. Out of Scope

- Multi-therapist or group-practice support
- Video / phone session hosting or telehealth links
- Insurance billing or superbill (itemised receipt for insurance reimbursement) generation
- Client-facing documents, worksheets, or homework sharing
- In-app chat or messaging between therapist and client
- Waitlist for cancelled slots
- Email reminders (SMS only per spec)
- Native iOS / Android app (web-first for V1)
- Variable pricing per session type or sliding-scale fees
- Therapist self-registration (account is created at setup, not through the app)

---

## 10. Success =

1. A brand-new client can create an account, complete the intake form, book a session, and pay — end to end — in under 5 minutes with no help from the therapist.
2. The therapist can open a completed session, write notes, and see them auto-saved within 60 seconds of finishing the appointment.
3. In the first 30 days of live use, zero session notes are accessible via any client account — confirmed by a deliberate security check (attempting to access note endpoints while authenticated as a client returns no note content).

---

## Context Carry

**One-liner:** Booking, payment, and private session notes for a solo licensed therapist.
**Roles:** Therapist (1 account — availability, all appointments, session notes); Client (register, intake form, book, pay, manage own appointments).
**Core loop:** Client registers → completes intake form → books slot → pays → attends → therapist writes session notes.
**V1 features:** Client Account, Intake Form, Availability & Booking, Per-Session Payment, Cancellation Policy (24-hour fee), Session Notes, Text Reminders.
**Data entities:** User, Intake Form, Availability Slot, Appointment, Payment, Session Note.
**Sensitive data:** Medical history and medications (health data); session note content (clinical records); payment provider references (financial data). Legal/compliance review required before launch — not optional.

runs.response:
# TherapyFlow — Spec

---

## 1. One-liner
A solo therapist's practice tool: clients book and pay for sessions online, the therapist manages her schedule and writes confidential session notes.

---

## 2. Users & Roles

| Role | What they can do | What they must NEVER be able to do |
|------|------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Therapist** (one account) | Log in; add and remove available time slots; set session price; view all bookings and payment statuses; view any client's profile and intake form; write, edit and read session notes; view SMS delivery logs | Read another practitioner's data (only one exists, but the rule stands for future safety) |
| **Client** | Create an account; complete and update their own intake form; browse available slots; book and pay for a session; cancel their own upcoming bookings; view their own booking history | Read session notes — theirs or anyone else's; view other clients' data; reach any therapist-only screen or URL |

---

## 3. The Core Loop

1. Client creates an account (name, email, phone number, password).
2. Client completes the intake form before accessing anything else.
3. Client browses open time slots and selects one.
4. Client pays for the session; the slot is reserved only after payment succeeds.
5. Client and therapist's calendar both reflect the confirmed booking.
6. Client receives SMS confirmation, then reminders 24 h and 1 h before the session.
7. Client attends the session.
8. Therapist writes session notes; these are visible to the therapist only, never the client.

---

## 4. Features — V1 (must ship)

> **Note on feature count:** Booking and payment form a single uninterrupted flow (the slot is not reserved until payment succeeds), so they are written as one feature. This keeps V1 at exactly 7 features.

---

**1. Client Accounts**
*As a client, I want to create an account so that I can book sessions and be recognized across visits.*

- [ ] Sign-up form collects: first name, last name, email, phone number, password.
- [ ] Duplicate email shows: *"An account with this email already exists."*
- [ ] Password shorter than 8 characters shows: *"Password must be at least 8 characters."*
- [ ] After sign-up, the client is taken straight to the intake form; the booking screen is inaccessible until the form is submitted.
- [ ] Login with correct credentials shows the client dashboard.
- [ ] Login with wrong credentials shows: *"Email or password is incorrect."* (Neither field is identified separately — this prevents an attacker from discovering whether an email is registered.)
- [ ] Any page that requires login redirects an unauthenticated visitor to the login screen.
- [ ] "Forgot password" link on the login screen sends a reset link to the client's registered email; the link expires after 1 hour; using an expired link shows: *"This link has expired. Please request a new one."*

---

**2. Intake Form**
*As a client, I want to fill in my medical background once so that my therapist has the context she needs before our first session.*

- [ ] Form collects: current medications (free text), relevant medical history (free text), reason for seeking therapy (free text, **required**), emergency contact name (text), emergency contact phone (text).
- [ ] Submitting without "reason for seeking therapy" shows: *"Please tell us why you're seeking therapy."*
- [ ] A client who has never submitted the form and tries to reach the booking screen sees: *"Please complete your intake form first."*
- [ ] Successful submission shows: *"Intake form saved."*
- [ ] Client can return and edit at any time; saving overwrites the previous version.
- [ ] Each free-text field accepts up to 5,000 characters; typing beyond the limit is blocked and a character counter shows what remains.
- [ ] Therapist can view the intake form from the client's profile.
- [ ] Intake form content never appears on any client-facing booking or history screen.

---

**3. Availability Management**
*As the therapist, I want to set which time slots are open so that clients can only book when I'm available.*

- [ ] Therapist adds a slot by choosing a date and start time; duration defaults to 50 minutes and is not editable in V1.
- [ ] Therapist can delete any open (not yet booked) slot; it disappears from the client calendar immediately.
- [ ] Attempting to delete a booked slot shows: *"This slot has a booking. Cancel the booking first."*
- [ ] Slots shown to clients are labeled in the therapist's configured time zone (e.g., *"Mon 28 Sep · 10:00 AM EDT"*).
- [ ] Slots whose start time is in the past are hidden from the client-facing calendar.
- [ ] Therapist sets a single global session price (whole dollar amount, stored in cents). Saving shows: *"Session price updated."*
- [ ] If no session price has been set, the client-facing booking screen shows: *"Online booking is not available yet."* and cannot be proceeded through.

---

**4. Booking & Payment**
*As a client, I want to choose a time slot and pay in one flow so that my session is confirmed the moment I pay.*

- [ ] Client sees only future, available (not yet booked) slots.
- [ ] Selecting a slot takes the client to a payment screen showing date, time, and price before any card entry.
- [ ] Card details are entered via the payment processor's hosted form; the app never stores card numbers, CVV, or expiry. ("Hosted form" means the payment company's own secure page handles card entry, not ours.)
- [ ] The slot is not reserved until payment succeeds; a failed payment leaves the slot available.
- [ ] If a slot is taken by another client between selection and payment (a "race condition" — two people acting on the same slot at the same moment), the client sees: *"This slot was just taken — please choose another,"* and is returned to the calendar; no charge is made.
- [ ] A client who already has a booking on the same calendar date cannot book a second slot that day; attempting to do so shows: *"You already have a session booked on this date."*
- [ ] After successful payment, the booking appears in the client's *Upcoming Sessions* list with status *Confirmed* and payment status *Paid.*
- [ ] Therapist's dashboard shows all bookings with client name, date/time, and payment status.

---

**5. SMS Reminders & Confirmations**
*As a client, I want text message reminders so that I don't miss my session.*
*As the therapist, I want clients reminded automatically so that I have fewer no-shows.*

- [ ] Client receives an SMS on booking confirmation containing: therapist name, date, time, and a note that cancellations within 24 hours are charged the full fee.
- [ ] Client receives an SMS reminder 24 hours before session start.
- [ ] Client receives an SMS reminder 1 hour before session start.
- [ ] Client receives an SMS when a booking is cancelled, stating whether a fee was charged.
- [ ] If any SMS fails to deliver, the failure is logged and a warning appears on the relevant booking in the therapist's dashboard — no silent failures, no crash.
- [ ] Therapist does not receive SMS reminders.

---

**6. Cancellation & Late-Cancellation Fee**
*As a client, I want to cancel a session I can't attend.*
*As the therapist, I want clients who cancel late to be charged so that my time is protected.*

- [ ] Client can cancel any upcoming booking from their *Upcoming Sessions* list.
- [ ] Cancellation **more than 24 hours** before start: session fee is fully refunded; booking status becomes *Cancelled — Refunded.*
- [ ] Cancellation **24 hours or fewer** before start: full session fee is charged (no refund); booking status becomes *Cancelled — Fee Charged.*
- [ ] Before confirming a late cancellation, client sees: *"Cancelling now will charge you the full session fee of $[amount]. Do you want to continue?"* with *Confirm* and *Go Back* buttons.
- [ ] If the late-cancellation charge itself fails to process, the cancellation does not complete and the client sees: *"We couldn't process the cancellation fee. Please contact your therapist."*
- [ ] After a successful cancellation, the slot becomes available for other clients.
- [ ] Therapist can view cancellation timestamp and fee status on each cancelled booking.

---

**7. Session Notes**
*As the therapist, I want to write private notes after each session so that I can track client progress over time.*

- [ ] On the therapist's dashboard, a *Write Notes* button appears on a booking once its scheduled start time has passed.
- [ ] Notes are free text, limited to 10,000 characters; a live character counter is shown.
- [ ] Notes auto-save every 30 seconds while the therapist is typing; a *Saved* indicator updates after each auto-save.
- [ ] Therapist can edit notes at any time after they are first created.
- [ ] Navigating away from a note with unsaved changes shows a browser warning: *"You have unsaved changes."*
- [ ] Therapist can view all notes for a client in chronological order from the client's profile page.
- [ ] No client-facing screen, URL, or API endpoint (a URL the app's code calls behind the scenes to fetch data) ever returns session note content — not even partially. Verifying this is a required part of acceptance testing before the app goes live.

---

## 5. Features — Later (explicitly NOT in V1)

| Feature | Why deferred |
|---------|-------------|
| Therapist cancels or reschedules on behalf of client | Adds refund-rule edge cases not needed to prove the core loop. |
| Recurring / package bookings | Per-session payment proves the loop; packages add payment complexity without new learning. |
| Waitlist for fully-booked days | No evidence of demand until V1 is live. |
| External calendar sync (Google Calendar, iCal) | Integration work; not part of the core loop. |
| Client-facing invoice downloads | Useful, but the core loop doesn't require it at launch. |
| Recurring weekly availability templates | Adding individual slots is enough to validate scheduling in V1. |
| Email reminders as SMS fallback | SMS alone is sufficient to test reminder behavior. |
| In-app messaging (therapist ↔ client) | Out-of-session communication is scope creep for V1. |
| Multiple therapist accounts | Explicitly a solo-practitioner product. |

---

## 6. Screens

### Client-facing

| Screen | Purpose | What's on it | Where you can go from here |
|--------|---------|-------------|---------------------------|
| **Sign Up** | Create an account | First/last name, email, phone, password fields; *Sign Up* button; link to Log In | → Intake Form |
| **Log In** | Return to account | Email, password; *Log In* button; *Forgot password* link; link to Sign Up | → Client Dashboard |
| **Intake Form** | Collect medical background (gate before booking) | Medications, medical history, reason for therapy (required), emergency contact fields; *Save* button | → Client Dashboard (after first save) |
| **Client Dashboard** | Overview of upcoming sessions | List of upcoming bookings (date, time, status); *Book a Session* button; *Edit Intake Form* link; empty state if no bookings | → Book a Session; Intake Form; Booking Detail |
| **Book a Session** | Browse and select an available slot | List or calendar of open future slots labeled with date, time, and price; empty state if none available | → Payment |
| **Payment** | Pay for the selected slot | Session summary (date, time, price); payment processor's card-entry form; *Pay* button; *Go Back* link | → Client Dashboard (success); Book a Session (failure or slot taken) |
| **Booking Detail** | View a single booking's status | Date, time, status, payment status; *Cancel* button (if upcoming) | → Cancellation Confirmation; Client Dashboard |
| **Cancellation Confirmation** | Confirm cancellation with fee warning if within 24 h | Warning message (with fee amount if applicable); *Confirm* and *Go Back* buttons | → Client Dashboard (after confirm); Booking Detail (Go Back) |

### Therapist-facing

| Screen | Purpose | What's on it | Where you can go from here |
|--------|---------|-------------|---------------------------|
| **Therapist Log In** | Authenticate the therapist | Email, password; *Log In* button | → Therapist Dashboard |
| **Therapist Dashboard** | Daily view and quick access | Upcoming bookings (client name, date/time, payment status); SMS failure warnings; *Write Notes* button on past sessions | → Booking Detail; Session Notes; Client Profile; Availability Management |
| **Availability Management** | Set open slots and session price | Calendar/date-picker to add a slot; list of existing slots with *Delete* buttons; session price field with *Save* button | → Therapist Dashboard |
| **Booking Detail (Therapist)** | Full booking record | Client name, date/time, status, payment status, cancellation info if applicable, SMS delivery status for this booking | → Client Profile; Session Notes |
| **Client Profile** | Full client record | Name, contact info; intake form (read-only); list of all bookings with links; list of all session notes | → Session Notes; Booking Detail |
| **Session Notes** | Write or edit notes for a session | Text area (10,000 char limit with counter); auto-save indicator; session date and client name as heading | → Client Profile; Therapist Dashboard |
| **Settings** | Configure practice details | Session price field; time zone selector; *Save* button | → Therapist Dashboard |

---

## 7. Data

> ⚠️ Fields marked **[SENSITIVE — HEALTH]** contain health information. Fields marked **[SENSITIVE — FINANCIAL]** contain financial data. Both types are subject to privacy laws (such as HIPAA in the United States and equivalent laws elsewhere). A qualified privacy attorney or compliance specialist must review data handling, storage, and access controls before this app launches. **This is not legal advice.**

### Client

| Field | Type | Who can read | Who can edit |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------|
| id | unique identifier | system | — |
| first_name | text | client (own), therapist | client |
| last_name | text | client (own), therapist | client |
| email | text (unique) | client (own), therapist | client |
| phone_number | text | client (own), therapist | client |
| password_hash | text | system only | system (on reset) |
| created_at | date/time | therapist | — |

### IntakeForm

| Field | Type | Who can read | Who can edit |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------|

## 8. Edge Cases & Empty States

1. **New client, no bookings yet** — Client Dashboard shows: *"You haven't booked a session yet."* with a prominent *Book a Session* button.
2. **Therapist has set no availability slots** — Booking screen shows: *"No sessions are available right now — check back soon."* No calendar or slots are rendered.
3. **Session price not set** — Booking screen shows: *"Online booking is not available yet."* Client cannot proceed; therapist sees a prompt in Settings.
4. **Slot taken mid-flow (race condition** — two clients acting on the same slot at the same instant**)** — Client sees: *"This slot was just taken — please choose another,"* is returned to the calendar, and no charge is attempted.
5. **Payment fails** — Client sees: *"Payment failed — please try a different card."* Slot stays available; no booking record is created.
6. **Late-cancellation fee charge fails** — Cancellation does not complete; client sees: *"We couldn't process the cancellation fee. Please contact your therapist."* Booking remains in its original state.
7. **Client tries to access session notes via direct URL** — Returns a permission-denied response (HTTP 403 — a standard "you're not allowed" code). Zero note content is returned, not even an error that names the note.
8. **Very long text** — Intake form fields block input beyond 5,000 characters; session notes block input beyond 10,000 characters; a live counter shows remaining characters in both cases.
9. **First-time user (intake form gate)** — A client who closes the tab without submitting the intake form is redirected back to it on next login; the booking screen is unreachable until submission.
10. **SMS delivery failure** — The failure is recorded in SMSLog; a warning badge appears on the affected booking in the therapist's dashboard. The booking and payment are unaffected.
11. **Therapist tries to delete a booked slot** — Shows: *"This slot has a booking. Cancel the booking first."* Slot is not deleted.
12. **Duplicate booking on same date** — If a client already has a booking on a given date and selects another slot on the same date, they see: *"You already have a session booked on this date."* before reaching payment.

---

## 9. Out of Scope

- Multiple therapist accounts or clinic/team features
- Therapist-initiated cancellation or rescheduling
- Client-facing invoice downloads or billing history
- Video or phone call links generated by the app
- Native mobile app (iOS or Android) — web browser only in V1
- Waitlists for fully-booked days
- External calendar sync (Google Calendar, iCal, Outlook)
- Email as a notification channel
- In-app messaging between therapist and client
- Two-factor authentication (a second login step, e.g. a code sent to your phone) — web authentication basics only in V1
- HIPAA / legal compliance configuration tooling — see Section 7; this requires a qualified professional and must not be treated as optional before launch

---

## 10. Success =

1. A new client completes the full loop — sign up → intake form → book → pay — without outside help, in a single browser session.
2. In QA testing (quality assurance — checking the finished product before release), a logged-in client account cannot retrieve session note content from any screen, URL, or API endpoint — zero exceptions, verified before launch.
3. The therapist can locate a client's profile, read their intake form, and open the session notes editor in 3 clicks or fewer from the dashboard.

---

## Context Carry

**One-liner:** A solo therapist's practice tool — clients book and pay for sessions online; the therapist manages her schedule and writes confidential session notes.
**Roles:** Therapist (one account, full control); Client (self-serve booking/payment, zero access to notes or other clients' data).
**Core loop:** Client signs up → completes intake form → selects slot → pays → attends → therapist writes session notes.
**V1 features:** Client Accounts, Intake Form, Availability Management, Booking & Payment, SMS Reminders & Confirmations, Cancellation & Late-Cancellation Fee, Session Notes.
**Data entities:** Client, IntakeForm, AvailabilitySlot, Booking, Payment, SessionNote, SMSLog, TherapistSettings.
**Sensitive data:** IntakeForm (medications, medical history, reason for therapy) and SessionNote (content) = health data; Payment and Booking payment_status = financial data. Privacy/legal review required before launch — not legal advice.

# TherapyBook — Spec

*(Working name — change it any time.)*

---

## 1. One-liner
A private, per-session booking and confidential session-notes tool for a solo licensed therapist: clients book and pay online, the therapist runs their practice and keeps secure notes.

---

## 2. Users & Roles

| Role | What they can do | What they must NEVER be able to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Therapist** | Log in; set and block availability; view all appointments; view any client's profile and intake form; write, read, and edit session notes; view payment status for every appointment | Modify payment amounts directly (the payment system controls this); permanently delete session notes or appointment records |
| **Client** | Create an account; complete and update their own intake form; browse available slots and book; pay per session; cancel their own appointments; view their own upcoming and past appointments | Read session notes (theirs or anyone else's); view another client's profile, intake form, or appointments; alter the therapist's availability |

> **Note:** The therapist account is created once during setup — there is no self-service sign-up for the therapist role.

---

## 3. The Core Loop

1. Client creates an account (email, phone, password).
2. On first login, client is shown the intake form and must complete it before booking.
3. Client browses available time slots and selects one.
4. Client reads the cancellation policy, acknowledges it, and pays upfront.
5. Both client and therapist receive an SMS *(Short Message Service — a text message)* confirmation.
6. 24 hours before the appointment, both receive an SMS reminder.
7. Client attends the session.
8. Therapist opens the completed appointment and writes confidential session notes.

---

## 4. Features — V1 (must ship)

**1. Client Accounts & Intake Form**
*As a client, I want to create an account and fill in my intake form so that the therapist has my background before our first session.*

- [ ] Sign-up requires: full name, email, phone number, password.
- [ ] After first login the intake form is shown immediately; client cannot reach the booking screen until the form is submitted.
- [ ] Intake form fields: date of birth, medical history (free text), current medications (free text), emergency contact name, emergency contact phone.
- [ ] Intake form displays a privacy notice explaining the data is confidential and used only by the therapist.
- [ ] Client must tick a consent checkbox before submitting the intake form.
- [ ] After submission, client can view and update their own intake form at any time from their account.
- [ ] Therapist can view any client's full intake form from the client's profile.

---

**2. Therapist Availability**
*As the therapist, I want to set and manage my bookable time slots so that clients can only book times I am free.*

- [ ] Therapist can define a recurring weekly schedule (e.g. Mon–Fri, 9 am–5 pm) broken into one-hour slots.
- [ ] Therapist can block individual slots or entire days.
- [ ] Slots already booked by a client are shown as unavailable; the therapist cannot edit them.
- [ ] Changes to availability do not affect already-confirmed appointments.
- [ ] When no slots are configured, the client's booking screen shows: *"No times available — please check back soon."*

---

**3. Appointment Booking**
*As a client, I want to browse available times and book one so that I can secure my session.*

- [ ] Client sees a calendar or list showing only open slots.
- [ ] Selecting a slot shows the session price before any payment is taken.
- [ ] If two clients try to book the same slot simultaneously *(a race condition — when two things happen at the exact same moment and clash)*, only one succeeds; the other sees: *"That time was just taken — please choose another."*
- [ ] Confirmed booking appears immediately in the client's Upcoming Appointments list.
- [ ] Therapist's dashboard updates immediately to show the new booking.
- [ ] Client receives an SMS confirmation after booking.

---

**4. Per-Session Payment & Cancellation Policy**
*As a client, I want to pay for my session at booking and understand the refund rules so that I know what I am committing to.*

- [ ] Full session fee is collected at the time of booking.
- [ ] Before payment, the cancellation policy is shown in plain text: *"Cancel more than 24 hours before your appointment for a full refund. Cancel within 24 hours and the session fee is non-refundable."*
- [ ] Client must tick a checkbox acknowledging the policy before the Pay button is active.
- [ ] If payment fails, no booking is created and the client sees: *"Payment failed — please check your card details and try again."* The slot remains available.
- [ ] Cancellations made more than 24 hours before the appointment trigger an automatic full refund.
- [ ] Cancellations made within 24 hours do not trigger a refund; the therapist retains the fee.
- [ ] Payment status (Paid / Refunded / Forfeited) is visible to the therapist on each appointment's detail view.
- [ ] After successful payment, the client sees a confirmation with the amount charged.

---

**5. SMS Reminders**
*As a client, I want a text reminder before my appointment so that I don't forget it.*

- [ ] Client receives an SMS 24 hours before the appointment.
- [ ] Therapist receives an SMS 1 hour before each appointment, showing the client's name and appointment time.
- [ ] No reminder is sent for cancelled appointments.
- [ ] If an SMS fails to send, the failure is logged but the appointment is unaffected; no error is shown to the client.

---

**6. Session Notes**
*As the therapist, I want to write private notes after each session so that I have a confidential record.*

- [ ] Session notes become editable once the appointment's scheduled time has passed.
- [ ] Notes are free text with a maximum of 10,000 characters per session.
- [ ] Notes auto-save every 30 seconds and on loss of focus *(when the therapist clicks elsewhere or switches tabs)*; a "Last saved [time]" indicator is shown.
- [ ] Notes are never shown to the client under any circumstances — no route, no link, no error message exposes them.
- [ ] Therapist can edit notes for any past appointment at any time.
- [ ] If no notes exist yet, the field shows placeholder text: *"No notes yet."*

---

**7. Therapist Dashboard**
*As the therapist, I want a single view of my day and client list so that I can manage my practice at a glance.*

- [ ] Dashboard shows today's appointments in time order: client name and appointment time.
- [ ] Dashboard shows the count of appointments scheduled for the current week.
- [ ] Therapist can navigate from any appointment to the client's profile (intake form + appointment history).
- [ ] Therapist can navigate from any past appointment to its session notes.
- [ ] Empty state — no appointments today: *"No appointments today."*
- [ ] Client list shows all clients alphabetically with their most recent appointment date.
- [ ] Client list shows *"No clients yet"* when empty.

---

## 5. Features — Later (explicitly NOT in V1)

| Feature | Reason deferred |
|---|---|
| Recurring / standing appointments | Single-session booking proves the core loop; recurring logic adds significant scheduling complexity. |
| Email reminders | SMS was explicitly requested; doubling up means a second integration before launch. |
| PDF receipts / invoices | On-screen confirmation covers V1; useful for insurance reimbursement but not core. |
| Intake form change history / audit log | V1 stores the latest version only; history is a compliance enhancement for later. |
| Waitlist for cancelled slots | Useful but not part of the core loop for V1. |
| Notes templates (SOAP, DAP, etc.) | Free text is enough to validate the feature; templates are a polish addition. |
| Client-to-therapist in-app messaging | Out of scope — not in the core loop. |
| Two-factor authentication | Good security practice; adds sign-in friction; prioritise after launch. |
| Multi-therapist / group practice support | The product is explicitly solo-therapist. |
| Telehealth / video integration | Not requested. |

---

## 6. Screens

### Client-facing

| **Sign Up** | Create a new client account | Name, email, phone, password fields; Submit button | → Intake Form |
| **Log In** | Returning client signs in | Email, password, Forgot-password link | → Intake Form (if not yet completed) or My Appointments |
| **Intake Form** | Capture health background before first booking | Date of birth, medical history (text area), medications (text area), emergency contact fields, privacy notice, consent checkbox, Submit button | → Book Appointment (after submission) |
| **Book Appointment** | Browse and select an available slot | Calendar or slot list showing open times, session price | → Payment |
| **Payment** | Pay and acknowledge cancellation policy | Appointment summary (date, time, price), cancellation policy text, policy checkbox, card details, Pay & Confirm button | → Booking Confirmation (success) or back (failure) |
| **Booking Confirmation** | Confirm the booking succeeded | Appointment date/time, amount charged, note about SMS reminder | → My Appointments |
| **My Appointments** | See upcoming and past appointments | Tabs: Upcoming / Past; list of appointments with date, time, status; Cancel button on upcoming items | → Appointment Detail (Client) |
| **Appointment Detail (Client)** | See one appointment's full details | Date, time, status, amount paid, cancellation policy reminder, Cancel Appointment button | → Cancellation Confirmation |
| **Cancellation Confirmation** | Confirm cancellation intent | Appointment info, refund eligibility based on timing, Confirm Cancellation and Keep Appointment buttons | → My Appointments |
| **Account / Profile** | Manage account and update intake form | Name, email, phone (editable), link to view/edit intake form, Log Out button | → Intake Form (to update) |

### Therapist-facing

|---|---|---|---|
| **Therapist Log In** | Therapist signs in | Email, password, Log In button | → Dashboard |
| **Dashboard** | At-a-glance view of today and this week | Today's appointments (time, client name), weekly count, links to Schedule and Client List | → Appointment Detail (Therapist), Schedule, Client List |
| **Schedule / Availability** | Manage bookable slots | Calendar view, Set Recurring Hours button, Block Slot / Block Day controls, confirmed bookings highlighted | → Appointment Detail (Therapist), Dashboard |
| **Client List** | Browse all clients | Alphabetical list with last appointment date, search bar | → Client Profile |
| **Client Profile** | Full view of one client | Name, email, phone, full intake form, appointment history | → Appointment Detail (Therapist) |
| **Appointment Detail (Therapist)** | Manage one appointment | Client name, date/time, payment status, link to session notes | → Session Notes, Client Profile |
| **Session Notes** | Write and review notes for one session | Appointment header (client name, date), notes text area, auto-save indicator, last-saved timestamp | → Appointment Detail (Therapist) |

---

## 7. Data

> **⚠️ Privacy & legal notice — applies to all sensitive fields below:** The app stores health information (medical history, medications, session notes), financial details (payment records), and personal data (name, phone, date of birth). This kind of data is subject to regulations such as HIPAA in the United States or equivalent laws elsewhere. ## 8. Edge Cases & Empty States

1. **No appointments yet — client:** "My Appointments" shows: *"You haven't booked a session yet. [Book your first session]."*
2. **No appointments today — therapist:** Dashboard shows: *"No appointments today."*
3. **Slot taken at the same moment by two clients (race condition):** Only one booking is confirmed. The other client immediately sees: *"That time was just taken — please choose another slot."*
4. **Payment fails at booking:** No appointment is created. Slot stays open. Client sees: *"Payment failed — please check your card details and try again."* App checks whether the charge went through before showing this message to prevent double-charging.
5. **Cancellation within 24 hours:** Before confirming, client sees: *"Cancellations within 24 hours of your appointment are non-refundable. Are you sure you want to cancel?"* On confirmation, fee is forfeited.
6. **Cancellation more than 24 hours before:** Refund is triggered automatically. Client sees: *"Your appointment has been cancelled and a full refund has been issued. Please allow 5–10 business days for it to appear."*
7. **Client tries to book before completing intake form:** App intercepts and redirects to the intake form with the message: *"Please complete your intake form before booking."*
8. **First-time client, no therapist availability set yet:** After completing the intake form, the booking screen shows: *"No times available — please check back soon."* No broken page.

10. **SMS reminder fails to send:** Failure is logged in the SMS Log; the appointment is not affected. No error is shown to the client or therapist at the time (a future admin view can surface this).
11. **Client account deleted while a future appointment exists:** The appointment record is preserved in the therapist's schedule, labelled *"Client account deleted."* Session notes are retained.
12. **Slow or offline connection during payment:** If no response arrives within 15 seconds, client sees: *"Something went wrong — please check your connection and try again."* The app re-checks payment status before treating it as failed, to avoid double-charging.

2. The therapist can open any completed appointment and read or write session notes, and those notes are completely inaccessible from the client's account by any path.
